discovery: Discovery of intrinsic long-range magnetism in atomically thin van der Waals crystals

nominees.name: Xiang Zhang
nominees.affiliation: The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong

motivation: In 2017, magneto-optical experiments on monolayer CrI3 (Xu, Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers) and on few-layer Cr2Ge2Te6 (Zhang and co-workers) showed that long-range magnetic order persists down to the atomically thin limit. This settled a long-standing question raised by the Mermin-Wagner theorem: magnetic anisotropy stabilizes order in two dimensions. The work created the field of van der Waals magnets. It revealed layer-dependent antiferromagnetism, electrically switchable magnetism, giant tunneling magnetoresistance in spin-filter junctions, and magnetic proximity control of other 2D materials. These crystals are now a platform for studying magnons, magnetoelectric coupling, excitons locked to spin order, and 2D multiferroicity. Magnetic order can be designed and controlled layer by layer. Nearly a decade on, hundreds of groups worldwide rely on these discoveries, which have opened a new window on quantum magnetism and spin-based devices.
